text:
There is a brush that sings upon the wall,
with new rhythm, old realities.
It brings ancient clarities to the present,
heightens a dark present in shadows.

But it is a brush named for the future,
and whatever it touches in life is changed.
To give shape to an idea it deforms
into great eyes, into immense fists.

It is a brush of old and new make,
the brush of always, the true one,
which in every age finds its timber,
bold and timely at once.

It is a brave brush, a pure brush
that stoops to no false charity;
it paints truths, works for truth,
steady its pulse, its heart secure.

It is a sincere brush and I try
to say what its fiber longs for and feels:
to always have that hand and that brow
that carry it singing across the wall.

translation.title: To the Brush on the Wall
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish original. The sonnet-like quatrains and the brush’s political and ethical force are preserved.
